title: The General Ledger
summary: The purpose of the General Ledger, debit and credit sides, the double-entry principle, posting CRJ and CPJ totals to ledger accounts, balancing the Bank account, and the Trial Balance.

notes.text: The **General Ledger** is the main book of the business. It contains a separate **account** for every item (Bank, Capital, Equipment, Current income, Wages and so on). Information from the journals is **posted** (transferred) to the ledger accounts, usually as monthly totals.
Each account has two sides: the left side is the **debit (Dr)** side and the right side is the **credit (Cr)** side.

notes.label: Key rule
notes.text: Every transaction is recorded in **two accounts**: once on the **debit** side of one account and once on the **credit** side of another, for the same amount. So total debits always equal total credits.

notes.caption: Which side increases each type of account?

items: **CRJ**: the Bank total is **debited** to the Bank account (money comes in). Each other column total is **credited** to its account (e.g. Current income Cr). Each sundry item is credited separately (e.g. Capital Cr, Loan Cr).

**CPJ**: the Bank total is **credited** to the Bank account (money goes out). Each other column total is **debited** to its account (e.g. Wages Dr, Stationery Dr). Each sundry item is debited separately (e.g. Equipment Dr, Drawings Dr).

notes.caption: Bank account (B1) of Thandi's Hair Salon, March 2025

notes.text: To **balance** an account, find the difference between the two sides, write it on the smaller side as 'Balance c/d' (carried down) so that both sides have the same total, then bring it down on the opposite side on the first day of the next month as 'Balance b/d' (brought down).
A **Trial Balance** lists the balances of all ledger accounts in two columns: **debit balances** and **credit balances**. If the double-entry was done correctly, the two totals are equal.

notes.caption: Trial Balance of Thandi's Hair Salon on 31 March 2025

questions.memo:
✓ c/d: carried down; the balance written on the smaller side to make both sides equal at month-end (1)
✓ b/d: brought down; the balance shown on the opposite side at the start of the next month (1)

questions.prompt: The CPJ shows Bank R9 000, Wages R6 000 and Sundry accounts: Equipment R3 000. Show how these totals are posted to the ledger.
questions.memo:
✓ Bank account credited R9 000 (1)
✓ Wages account debited R6 000 (1)
✓ Equipment account debited R3 000 (1)

questions.prompt: What is a Trial Balance and why is it drawn up?
questions.memo:
✓ A list of all ledger account balances in debit and credit columns (1)
✓ to check that total debits equal total credits (double entry correct) (1)
